svg.title: R environments: the enclosure chain from the workspace to the empty environment, and the three environments of a function call
svg.desc: Two panels. The left panel shows the search path as a chain of environments, each the enclosure of the one above it: R_GlobalEnv (the workspace), package:tools attached last with library(), the default packages stats, graphics, grDevices, utils, datasets and methods, Autoloads, the base environment, and finally R_EmptyEnv, which has no parent. Arrows labelled enclosure or parent.env() point from each environment to the next. The right panel shows a call to a function f() made from inside another function g(). The frame of f(), its execution environment holding arguments and local variables, has an arrow labelled enclosure or parent.env() to the definition environment of f, which is the environment where f was created and here is R_GlobalEnv, the top of the chain on the left, and a second dashed arrow labelled parent.frame() to the frame of g(), the calling environment. Free variables are looked up along the enclosure arrows only, never through parent.frame().
svg.text: Where R looks for a name, and which environment is which
The enclosure chain (search path)
each environment is the enclosure of the one above it
R_GlobalEnv
the workspace; top-level assignments land here
enclosure / parent.env()
package:tools
attached last with library(): position 2
package:stats ... package:methods
the default packages, in reverse order of attaching
Autoloads
proxy objects that are loaded on demand
package:base (baseenv())
the last entry of search(); locked since R 4.1.0
R_EmptyEnv (emptyenv())
no parent; nothing can be assigned in it
search()
One call to f(), made from inside g()
three environments, two different arrows
Frame of g(): the calling environment
where the call f() was evaluated; changes with
every call, so it is never part of a lookup chain
parent.frame()
Frame of f(): the execution environment
formal arguments and local variables; a new frame is
created for every call and lookup starts here
enclosure / parent.env()
environment(f): the definition environment
where function(...) was evaluated; fixed when f was
created. Here it is R_GlobalEnv, top of the chain
same environment
A free variable in f is looked for in the frame of f(),
then along the enclosure arrows (solid), up the chain at the left.
parent.frame() (dashed) only matters when code asks for it.
